I notice you have a yellowish tint to your skin and eyes, and you seem quite agitated. To understand what is causing these symptoms, have you been experiencing any pain in your right upper abdomen or fever recently?

speaker: Doctor
text: The labs confirm significant liver injury with elevated bilirubin and transaminases. Have you recently consumed large amounts of alcohol, taken any new medications, or experienced nausea and vomiting? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Profile; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound data is missing, but the labs confirm severe liver dysfunction with a significantly reduced albumin level. Have you been feeling unusually tired or sleepy recently, and have you noticed any confusion or changes in your mental status?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of substance use and high-risk behaviors, have you experienced any unintentional weight loss, night sweats, or swelling in your legs or abdomen?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis (likely due to substance use or viral etiology). The clinical picture of severe jaundice, markedly elevated transaminases, coagulopathy, and altered mental status (agitation/confusion) strongly indicates acute liver failure. Immediate admission for supportive care and evaluation for liver transplantation is required.
